opencode.json declares AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md as instructions, scripts/opencode-agents.py generates .opencode/agent/*.md from .claude/agents/*.md, add.sh runs it at install and verify.sh fails on drift. No skills symlink, no session-start plugin, no symlinked agents. Verified against opencode 1.18.25: all four agents resolve with mode subagent and the right tool denials, config resolves, a probe install into a fresh repo produces the lot. Two deviations from the design, both noted in .claude/HARNESS.md — instructions lists CLAUDE.md rather than .claude/HARNESS.md so opencode always-loads exactly what Claude Code does, and the generated agents carry no model: line (har-ctd). Skill discovery turns out to be racy in opencode itself: har-nvb.

harness update ships as a command, and add.sh now warns loudly instead of skipping quietly for contract files. Classification is read off the template's content — a '── FILL THIS IN' block means the project is meant to edit it (verify.sh, the reviewers, seat.md, dashboard.py), everything else is contract and exits non-zero when stale OR missing entirely, which is control-center-pro's absent opencode.json. Comparison normalises the installer's own post-copy edits (bd setup codex's AGENTS.md block, the tidier's json.dumps key reorder) or every fresh install read as stale; a gate step now holds that. Shared logic between add and update lives in commands/lib/install.sh. Dogfooding caught two bugs before review: the false-alarm-on-fresh-install, and the classifier grepping bare words so HARNESS.md demoted itself the moment it documented the rule. Both reviewers independently found only issues already fixed. Starter's own root drift filed as har-awe.

add.sh now registers the Dolt remote when bd init didn't (no origin at init time, or a ledger predating the step), deriving it from the target's own origin via harness_dolt_remote_url — bd rejects scp-style git@host:org/repo, so that form is rewritten to git+ssh://. Compared against the URL origin resolves to now, not just checked for the name, so a repo that changes host is re-pointed instead of silently pushing to the old remote. Gated on a real ledger rather than .beads existing, so a failed bd init doesn't get misreported as a remote problem. Nothing ever ran bd dolt push, so scripts/ledger-push.sh does it and the handoff procedure calls it. Verified end to end: install -> wire -> file bead -> push -> fresh clone -> bd dolt pull returns the bead. Findings out of scope: har-wan, har-7xb.
